newsitem.title: CHINA: China says underwriters need regulatory nod.
newsitem.headline: China says underwriters need regulatory nod.

text.p: China said on Thursday that securities companies that did not win special regulatory approval could not act as underwriters for stock or debt offerings after February next year.
All securities firms that wished to conduct underwriting activities needed certification that they were qualified by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Any securities firm that had a "serious violation" of securities regulations within the last year would not be given such permission for the time being, the agency said.

It also said that 10 securities firms, including China International Trust and Investment Corp's securities subsidiary, and Guangdong Development Securities Co, had been confirmed as qualified underwriters.
It did not say whether other firms would be approved before the cut-off date, which was set at February 15, 1997.
